messages.content: Can you please help me find some Hillbilly songs. I'd particularly enjoy something from the album Chief by Eric Church.

The user wants to find some Hillbilly songs, particularly from the album Chief by Eric Church. We have a function Music_3_LookupMusic that can retrieve a list of songs based on artist, album, genre, year. The user specifically wants songs from the album Chief by Eric Church. So we should call Music_3_LookupMusic with artist="Eric Church", album="Chief". The genre might be "Hillbilly"? But the function only accepts certain genres: "Reggae", "Holiday", "Electropop", "Pop", "Asia", "House", "Electronica", "Funk", "Rock", "Metal", "Dubstep", "Country", "dontcare". There's no "Hillbilly" but "Country" might be close. The user didn't specify a genre filter. So we can set genre to "dontcare" or "Country". The user didn't specify year. So we can set year to "dontcare". The function signature: Music_3_LookupMusic({artist: string, album: string, genre?: string, year?: number}). The defaults: artist default "dontcare", album default "dontcare", genre default "dontcare", year default "dontcare". So we need to provide artist and album. So we call:

Music_3_LookupMusic({
  artist: "Eric Church",
  album: "Chief",
  genre: "dontcare",
  year: "dontcare"
})

But the year expects a number or "dontcare". The default is "dontcare". So we can omit year. The function signature: year?: number. But the default is "dontcare". So we can omit year. So we call:

Music_3_LookupMusic({
  artist: "Eric Church",
  album: "Chief"
})

We also might want to specify genre: "Country" to narrow down. But the user didn't ask for that. They just want songs from the album Chief. So we can just call with artist and album. That should return a list of songs. Then we can present them to the user. The user might want to play them. But they didn't ask to play. They just asked to find. So we just return the list.
